transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I, uh... I guess I'm here because of work. I'm a cashier, and... my boss wrote me up last week. I just... I keep doing things at the register that don't really make sense. Like, I'll start tapping the scanner in this specific pattern, or I'll just... freeze. With my hand right over the cash drawer. Even when someone's standing right there waiting. It's just... happening a lot.
Right before this happens, do you notice a specific thought, worry, or urge that makes you feel like you have to do it, or does it just happen suddenly without any warning?
I... no. I don't really notice anything like that. It's not a worry or... anything. It just sort of happens. I don't really know.
During these moments when you're tapping the scanner or freezing, are you fully aware of what's happening around you, or do you lose track of time or consciousness?
I... I think I'm aware. I don't pass out or anything. I'm just... standing there. I see the customer. I just... I don't really know. I don't think I lose time.
When you're in the middle of the tapping or freezing, if someone touches your arm or calls your name, are you able to stop right away, or does it continue no matter what you or they do?

I... I don't really know. Nobody really touches my arm. If they say something, like "excuse me"... I'm not sure. I don't think I stop right away. I just... stay like that until it stops. I haven't really noticed.
When one of these episodes happens, about how long does it usually last—seconds, or more like a minute or longer?
I... I'm not really sure. I don't look at a clock or anything when it happens. Maybe a few seconds... maybe longer. I just... I haven't kept track.
After one of these episodes ends, do you feel completely normal right away, or do you notice confusion, extreme tiredness, or muscle soreness afterward?
I don't... I don't really feel anything special. I just go back to scanning. I don't think I'm confused or anything. Just... back to work.
Do these episodes only happen while you're at work at the register, or have you noticed similar tapping or freezing happening in other situations, like at home or when you're relaxed?

I think... mostly just at work. That's really why I came in. At the register, I just keep getting stuck doing things that don't fit the moment. Like the tapping on the scanner, or freezing with my hand right over the cash drawer while a customer is just standing there waiting. It... it got me written up last week.
Do these episodes tend to happen more when you're feeling stressed, anxious, or under pressure at work, like during a rush or a tense interaction with a customer?
I don't know... maybe. I haven't really paid attention to that. I just... it just happens. I don't think it matters if it's busy or not.
During or right after one of these episodes, have you ever noticed biting your tongue, losing control of your bladder or bowels, or getting injured?
No. Nothing like that. I haven't gotten hurt or... anything else.
Do these episodes ever happen when you're alone at the register with no customers or coworkers watching, or do they only seem to occur when someone is right there interacting with you?
I don't... I really don't know. There's almost always someone around somewhere, it's a store. I haven't really paid attention to who's watching me.
Have you ever noticed that if you try hard to concentrate on something else, or someone distracts you during one of these episodes, the tapping or freezing stops or lessens?
I haven't really noticed. I don't... I don't think I've ever tried to concentrate on something else when it happens. It just does what it does.
Has this tapping or freezing ever happened when you were completely alone—like in the break room, bathroom, or at home—where you're certain no one could see you at all?
I don't know. I... I haven't really kept track of it. When I'm at home, I just... I don't really think about it. I'm not sure if it happens then.
Has anyone ever noticed you having these tapping or freezing episodes while you were asleep, or do they only ever happen when you're awake?
I live alone. So... there's no one there to see if I do anything in my sleep. I just... I don't know.
When these tapping or freezing episodes happen, do they always look exactly the same each time—same movements, same pattern—or does the way they look change from one episode to the next?
I... I don't really pay that much attention to it. It's just... tapping. I don't know if it's exactly the same every time. I just want it to stop.
Do these episodes ever happen at the register when you're just scanning items with no customer waiting or watching you, or do they only seem to occur when you're actively interacting with someone?

It's... mostly when they're there. Waiting. I just get stuck doing things that don't really fit the moment. Like... tapping the scanner in a pattern. Or I'll just freeze with my hand hovering over the cash drawer while the customer is standing right there waiting for me. It's... well, I got written up for it last week. So... yeah. When they're there.
Right before or during these episodes, when a customer is standing there waiting, do you notice any feelings of anxiety, panic, or being overwhelmed in that moment?
I don't really... feel panicked, I guess. It's not like that. I just... it just happens. I'm not really paying attention to how I feel.
Have you noticed whether these episodes ever happen when you're talking with someone outside of work—like a friend, family member, or someone on the phone—not just with customers at the register?
I don't... I don't really talk to a lot of people outside of work. I mostly just keep to myself. So... no. I haven't noticed it happening then. Just at the store.

Does it seem like the tapping or freezing gets worse specifically when you notice someone is watching your hands or paying close attention to you, compared to when they're just standing nearby but not really looking at what you're doing?
I don't know. I haven't really... paid attention to where they're looking. I just know they're there. Waiting.
If you notice the tapping or freezing starting, and you consciously try as hard as you can to stop yourself or hold still, are you able to stop it, or does it continue no matter how hard you try?
I... I haven't really tried. I just... I just wait for it to be over. I don't think about stopping it. It just happens.
Does this tapping or freezing ever happen when you're doing other repetitive hand movements—like typing on a phone, writing, or using a keyboard—outside of scanning items at the register?
No... I don't really type or... use a keyboard much anymore. So, no. It's just... just at the register.
